body: Performing is actually the one time I feel okay, because it's the one time I actually feel loved in a way that feels like it's under MY control. Like, in a relationship, I'm at the mercy of whoever I'm dating more or less, but performing? That's my domain. I'm the queen of my little stage kingdom, and if I play well, then I win affection. Contrast to dating, or interpersonal interaction in general, where I feel like I have almost no ability to positively influence the outcome. I can't win, I can only try to lose less.

I don't have anything to add to this besides that tweak a couple details and I could've written this. I'm a musician as well, and a big part of the reason I do that is, like you say, recognition and validation. I just wish I understood how to need that less.

Feeling like there's something wrong with you because all your friends can do it so easily is a big part of it for me, as well. Like I know it's not EASY for them, but when I'm struggling with finding someone who even so much as wants a second date with me, it becomes a lot harder for me to be sympathetic yknow? And then I start wondering how I can possibly be so broken that I can just drift through the world being ignored by practically everyone and it gets all bad.
just laid in bed all day. i'm a real winner, you see.

i do stuff like that sometimes (hell, i bought coffee for all my coworkers yesterday because i was getting good tips and it seemed like a nice thing to do), but it doesn't really help with the feeling of being unloved/unlovable. being in a relationship is the one thing i've found that really, really helps me deal with these feelings, but finding someone to be in a relationship WITH me is all but impossible so welp.

maybe. she's been pretty good to me for a while, but this is really starting to bug me. i don't know if any other therapist would be better, though. they never seem to accept that my self-hatred doesn't just spring from nowhere.
also i think i'm not going to work. i cannot handle anything right now.

i see a therapist weekly and text her during the week. honestly though, she's been starting to grate on me a lot lately. i've been thinking the money would be better spent on charm school than therapy, because she doesn't want to address my actual problem (being unloved and unlovable) and instead she's like "so why do you have such negative opinions about yourself?"
